## Natural history notes

A large, fast-moving centipede characterized by its flattened body, many pairs of legs, long antennae, and bluish-green to dark green coloration. In Florida, it is found in moist sheltered habitats such as leaf litter, rotting logs, soil, mulch, gardens, hammocks, and other areas with ground cover. It is mostly active at night and feeds on insects, spiders, and other small invertebrates, using venomous front claws to subdue prey.
